candidate.derivedAnswer: C; the two vectors must not be collinear.
candidate.answerReason: Two noncollinear plane vectors form a basis. Collinear vectors cannot represent every vector in the plane.

methods.label: Basis condition
methods.explanation: Two collinear vectors cannot span the entire plane. Neither perpendicularity nor unit length is required.
methods.levelReason: Uses only the noncollinearity condition for a plane-vector basis.

candidate.changeReason: Noncollinearity is the necessary basis condition, while perpendicularity and unit length are unnecessary. The explanation sufficiently distinguishes C.

review.mathematicalCheck: Linear combinations of a collinear pair remain on one line and cannot cover the plane. Noncollinearity is therefore necessary, giving C. Unit length and perpendicularity are not necessary.
